page: Microsoft Azure L64s_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores using the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 512.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates 16,047 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark testing shows strong multi-threaded computational output and memory throughput. The server achieved strong tier results in multi-core stress-ng workloads, Geekbench multi-core evaluation, and PassMark CPU metrics. Large block uncached memory bandwidth reached 300.85 GB/sec for reads and 138.08 GB/sec for writes. Application benchmarks showed 62.34 million Redis SET operations per second and 54.74 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Single-threaded performance metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench measured in the average tier, while large parameter language model CPU inference registered weak generation throughput.

The dense pairing of 16,047 GB local NVMe storage and 512.0 GB RAM provides high resource efficiency for input-output heavy architectures without requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is aligned with high-performance transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, in-memory caching systems, and high-throughput static data processing.
